subject: Sparrow pilot — temporary throughput carve-out and 72h ramp forecast
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Lin <david@sparrow.ai>, platform-team@sparrow.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sparrow pilot: request for temporary throughput carve-out + 72h ramp forecast

Team — quick context: Sparrow is running a closed pilot next Tuesday and asked if we can provide a short-term throughput uplift (temporary quota carve-out) to support the first 72 hours of ramp. They are expecting a bursty pattern as they enable a new NLU feature; forecast attached.

Key numbers (from Sparrow product):
- Expected peak concurrent requests: 600–900 rps during 09:00–21:00 PDT windows (first 48h), settling to ~200 rps by hour 72.
- Avg tokens per request: 850 tokens (prompt + expected continuation).
- Estimated sustained token rate (peak): ~765k tokens/minute during top window.
- Streaming: ~30% of requests will use streaming responses.

Ask:
1) Can we allocate a temporary carve-out for Sparrow from our shared burst pool for 72 hours starting 2028-03-14 08:00 PDT?
2) If not full carve-out, what conservative uplift (% or absolute tokens/min) can infra provide without violating latency SLOs for other customers?
3) Product: any model variant recommendations or prompt-level caching we can use to reduce egress (e.g., disable non-essential context fetches)?

I attached Sparrow_72h_ramp.xlsx with their by-hour plan and a short MAP they shared. They’ve pushed the pilot date up and want a go/no-go by EOD today so they can finalize their rollout gating.

Next steps I propose:
- Product + Infra sync within 2 hours to scope risk and a fallback mapping sheet.
- If approved, ops to create a timeboxed entitlement and routing policy that auto-reverts after 72 hours.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sparrow pilot: request for temporary throughput carve-out + 72h ramp forecast

Thanks Marissa — skimmed the sheet. A few clarifying product asks before I can approve any carve-out:

1) Model choice: which model do they plan to hit? Are they on an Llama-3-34B-opt or a quantized 13B variant? The cost/latency delta is material and affects which pool we map them to.
2) Streaming vs non-streaming split: you listed ~30% streaming. If we assume streaming latency constraints, we need to reserve a lower-latency pool (dedicated nvlink-backed nodes). Confirm exact percent or give a 90th percentile estimate.
3) Prompt caching: can Sparrow precompute/static-cache the 40% of prompts that are identical? If so, effective token load drops significantly — please confirm with David offline and mark in the sheet.
4) Fallback policy: if we can’t grant full tokens/min, we should predefine fallback models (quantized 8-bit variants) and a progressive rate-limiter so user-facing errors are controlled.

From roadmap perspective: if they’re on the 34B-opt, we can probably give short-term 2.5x uplift without SLA exposure if infra disables background preemption and routes traffic to a reserved slice. If they’re on 13B-quant, 4x uplift is feasible.

I’ll carve out tentative model mapping options once Marissa confirms model, streaming %, and any ability to cache.

—Markus
Product (serving)
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sparrow pilot: request for temporary throughput carve-out + 72h ramp forecast

Looping infra constraints: we have a scheduled cluster maintenance on 2028-03-15 02:00–06:00 PDT that affects half of the shared burst pool (NVlink-backed). If Sparrow’s top window overlaps that maintenance we either need to:

- Move them to a different physical pool (capacity permitting) for the 72h window, or
- Shift the maintenance (needs approval from infra leads) or
- Limit the uplift to non-NVlink nodes which increases latency and may impact success rate.

Operationally I can:
- Provision a timeboxed dedicated slice on a GPU pool (estimated extra cost, needs finance approval if over X credits) — takes ~3 hours to configure once we have the exact model mapping and an IP allowlist.
- If we go with a progressive policy instead of a hard carve-out, I recommend we implement token-based throttles with rate-limited backpressure headers so Sparrow can gracefully retry.

I attached maintenance_window_schedule.pdf showing the maintenance footprint. If the team confirms model and streaming %, I’ll run a quick capacity fit and propose three options with associated risk/cost.

FYI: I can’t guarantee a full 4x uplift for Llama-34B during the 09:00–21:00 window unless we reserve a dedicated slice.

—Olga
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Lin <david@sparrow.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sparrow pilot: request for temporary throughput carve-out + 72h ramp forecast

Thanks all — consolidating to move fast. Decision path and immediate asks below.

Summary of constraints:
- Sparrow requests large, bursty uplift for pilot (sheet attached).
- Product (Markus) needs model variant + confirmed streaming % + caching confirmation to finalize mapping.
- Infra (Olga) flagged a maintenance window that could reduce available NVlink-backed capacity. Dedicated slice required for safest outcome.

Action items (owners & SLAs):
1) Marissa: confirm with David right now which model variant they will run ("34B-opt" or "13B-quant") and whether Sparrow can chunk/edge-cache ~40% of prompts; reply by 19:30 PDT. (owner: Marissa)
2) Markus: based on model variant, publish two mapping options (dedicated slice configuration + progressive fallback mapping to 8-bit) by 20:30 PDT. Put numbers for expected p99 latency and estimated tokens/min. (owner: Markus)
3) Olga: run capacity fit for both mapping options and return an explicit uplift recommendation (tokens/min and cost estimate) + whether we must move maintenance; deliver by 21:15 PDT. Note — if you propose dedicated slice, include config snippet and prep ETA. (owner: Olga)
4) Kimberly/Finance: if dedicated slice cost > $X credits/day, Kimberly to flag approval path and expedite finance sign-off. (owner: Kimberly)
5) Ops: if approved, create a timeboxed routing policy that auto-reverts at 2028-03-17 08:00 PDT and open JIRA-OPS-4217 for the change. (owner: Ops)

Contingency decision: if we can’t agree on dedicated slice by 21:30 PDT, we will provide a conservative progressive throttle (1.8x uplift) and pre-deploy fallback quantized models. That will be communicated to Sparrow (David) and must be implemented as an automated routing rule.

Links: HubSpot deal, drive folder with Sparrow materials, and JIRA-OPS-4217 are in the thread metadata. I will draft the external go/no-go note for David once infra + product numbers are in.

Marissa — please keep David in the loop on timings; we need external confirmation no later than 21:30 so they can lock rollout gates on their side.

Thanks — Lukas
Director, Customer Success
Lukas Meyer | lukas@redwood.ai
